name: Missouri
overview: Under Missouri law the county collector offers land with delinquent taxes at a public auction each year on the fourth Monday in August, starting at 10 o'clock, at or near the courthouse; the collector may also run it online at the same time. After payment the collector gives the buyer a certificate of purchase rather than a deed. The owner has an absolute right to redeem during the following year by paying the amount due plus interest at the rate in the certificate, not more than ten percent a year, and the right to redeem ends when the buyer gets the deed.

counties.how_to_bid: Register in person at the Collector's office before the day of sale (the county says no one may register on sale day; out-of-state bidders must be registered by the Wednesday before the sale). Missouri residents file a sworn, notarized affidavit with the Collector before the sale. The 2026 sale was held at the historic Cass County Courthouse, 102 E. Wall, Harrisonville; all bidders must be present. Properties go in the order published, the opening bid is at least the total back taxes, and raises are at least ten dollars. Pay the full bid at the end of the sale, no later than 2:00 p.m., by cashier's check, cash or credit card (fees apply); a defaulting purchaser owes a 25% penalty plus attorney's fees.

counties.how_to_bid: Bidder registration opens August 1 and closes on the Thursday before the sale. counties.how_to_bid: Bidders must be Missouri residents aged 18 or over (out-of-state bidders appoint a Missouri resident as agent) and give the Collector a signed, notarized bidder's affidavit stating they owe no delinquent property taxes; businesses must be registered in Missouri. Show Missouri ID to get a bid number: numbers are issued only the week before the sale and stop at 9 AM on sale day. The sale starts at 10:00am in the Assembly Room of the Administration Building in Hillsboro and bidders must be present. Properties go in newspaper order (1st, then 2nd, then 3rd offerings), the minimum bid is the taxes and sale expenses due, and the highest bidder wins. Pay at the Collector's office within 2 hours after all properties have been offered; failure to pay brings a 25% fine. The eligible property list is posted on the Collector's website in June.

counties.office: Office of the Sheriff, City of St. Louis (Land Tax Sales)
counties.address: 10 N. Tucker Blvd, 8th Floor, Civil Courts Building, St. Louis, MO 63101
counties.schedule_rule: The City of St. Louis holds land tax sales several times a year.
counties.next_sale_note: Land tax sales have concluded for the year. The last 2026 sale on the Collector's schedule was Sale 240 (October 6, 2026). 2027 dates not yet posted.
counties.how_to_bid: Pre-register online at least 10 days before the sale (one application per person or business); the Sheriff checks that the bidder has no delinquent city property taxes, unpaid special tax bills or pending building or housing code violations. Approved bidders get an email and pick up a bidder number on the first sale day with a valid State ID. Sales begin at 9:00 am outdoors on the 11th Street side of the Civil Courts Building, and bidding starts at the taxes owed. Pay by cashier's check or money order to 'Sheriff City of St. Louis' by 2:00 PM on the sale day, with a separate $150.00 payment per parcel; cash is no longer accepted.
